statement: For every nonempty finite graph G (possibly disconnected), every vertex k, and every integer n>=1, the integral homology of Sigma(G,{k},n) is torsion-free. More precisely, if c is the number of components and beta=rank H_1(G;Z), then rank H_q(Sigma(G,{k},n);Z)=binom(n,q) beta^q (c^(n-q)-(c-1)^(n-q)) for 0<=q<=n, with the rank at q=n equal to zero, and all higher homology zero. Consequently any torsion witness in the frozen problem must have |K|>=2 and n>=|K|+2.
contribution: A based-homotopy reduction identifies every singleton-anchor space with the fat wedge of a disjoint union of bouquets, whose product-cell differential is zero; this gives an exact all-graph rank formula and removes every singleton anchor from the torsion search. Exact Smith certificates for both diamond anchor orbits at n=3 cross-check the formula. Novelty remains subject to fresh literature review.
